name: Ramp
text: Add one high-contrast skip link at the very top of every page that jumps straight to the main content. This fixes the biggest keyboard navigation pain point for screen reader users and power keyboarders without cluttering the UI. The trade-off is a tiny bit of vertical space at the top of the page, but that’s negligible compared to the universal benefit.

name: Reader
text: Risk: A single skip link fails on pages with multiple distinct content sections—screen reader users must tab through the skip link repeatedly to reach different areas. Better alternative: Place a skip link at the top of each major content block (e.g., header, sidebar, main, footer) so users jump directly to their target. Settle this by testing with a screen reader on a page with multiple sections—if users still struggle, the alternative wins.

name: Reader
text: Risk: A single skip link forces all users—regardless of page structure—into the main content, ignoring pages with multiple distinct sections like dashboards or long forms. Better alternative: Add context-aware skip links that adapt to page structure, placing one at the top of each major content block (header, sidebar, main, footer). Settle this with a quick test: run a keyboard-only audit on a multi-section page and measure how many extra tabs users endure with each approach.
